solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A single beautiful being

parts.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a day' means per
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: Someone describes an attractive unmarried person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A single' reads as an unmarried person; it splits into PER (as in 'so much a head') and I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a fairy or lovely spirit, a gorgeous supernatural creature.

clue.text: Output from Sharpe in which lecturer's almost completely worn down

definitions.text: Output from Sharpe in which lecturer's almost completely worn down

parts.words: Output from Sharpe in which lecturer's almost completely worn down
parts.note: Tom Sharpe's comic novel follows Henry, a downtrodden further-education lecturer, and its title also means to droop or flag

explanation.surface: A description of a novel by Tom Sharpe about a ground-down lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Sharpe was an English comic novelist; his 1976 book is named after its hero, and the title word also means to go limp. The theme is famous people named Will.
explanation.definitionFit: The book title doubles as a verb for flagging or drooping, which suits a hero exhausted by his job.

clue.text: Why, perhaps, publicity stunt is screened

indicators.note: something screened is kept out of view, so the letters sit concealed inside the words Why, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a publicity stunt is being shown on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotional fuss or an exaggerated campaign drummed up to attract attention is exactly this.

clue.text: Out to get metal parts fixed

indicators.note: the metal parts the other word, splitting it open so the metal sits in the middle

parts.note: a picture fixed on a wall has been hung
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to have some metal components repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the hunt for someone means pursuing them, being out to get them.

clue.text: US space-traveller received in English county

indicators.note: one word placed in another, so the radio acknowledgement goes inside the county

parts.note: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, a county north-west of London
Roger is the radio word for 'message received'

explanation.surface: An American astronaut is welcomed in an English shire.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-strip and film hero is a twenty-fifth-century American spaceman.

clue.text: Film with Van Damme, you and I eying duo askance

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: looking askance means looking sideways or awry, so these letters are skewed into a new order

explanation.surface: Jean-Claude Van Damme and a pair of us eye two people suspiciously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'askance' turns EYING DUO into DIEYOUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: This 2019 action thriller stars Jean-Claude Van Damme, the Belgian martial-arts actor.

clue.text: Where player's putting club — Forest?

parts.note: a golfer putts on the green
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A golf scene: a player on the putting surface with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Greenwood is an England rugby player, part of the theme of Wills.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland in leaf, as in Robin Hood's haunt, is a poetic name for a forest.

clue.text: Tie is rearranged with United in case

indicators.note: the extra letter goes within the shuffled letters, sitting among them
the letters of Tie are put in a different order

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A tie is re-knotted for a United match, just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: City break with Fatima's husband a sign of neurosis?

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
hol is short for holiday, a break
Ali married Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad

explanation.surface: A city holiday with a historical figure might bring on nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode of the City, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: The compulsive repeating of others' words is a symptom seen in some psychiatric and developmental conditions.

clue.text: Being cut up during West End run?

definitions.meaning: having surgery in an operating room
a show running in London's West End is playing on stage

explanation.surface: Someone is upset during a long West End show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' looks like 'upset', but it means operated on; the West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery takes place in an operating suite, and a stage play is performed on stage, both called by the same phrase.

clue.text: Ted, for ever following Hearts

indicators.note: the word for ever comes after the card suit's letter

parts.note: H is the bridge abbreviation for hearts
aye or ay is an old word for always, for ever

explanation.surface: A man called Ted is a lifelong supporter of Hearts, the Edinburgh football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ted' looks like a name but is a farming verb: to ted is to spread mown grass to dry. Will Hay, the comic actor, is one of the theme's Wills.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedding mown grass turns it into dried fodder, so to make the dried grass is to ted.

clue.text: Individuals in school tremble after Head's expulsion

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, has been expelled from the word for tremble

parts.note: to tremble is to shake

explanation.surface: Pupils quake once the headteacher is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The school is of fish, not pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swim in schools, so one of these white fish is a member of a school.

clue.text: Like Rodin's second Thinker?

parts.note: e.g. (for example) means like

indicators.note: the second letter of the sculptor's name is taken

explanation.surface: A question about Rodin's famous sculpture The Thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The conscious self that does one's thinking, in Freudian terms, is the thinking part of the mind.

clue.text: Outlaw receives name of one supplying still bedding down in nursery

indicators.note: the word for outlaw takes in the credit line, holding it inside

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a byline is the credit naming the photographer who supplied a still picture

explanation.surface: A bandit takes in the name of a moonshiner, then beds down in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' suggests a distillery; it is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and pillowcases for a cot or crib are the infants' bedclothes, found in a nursery.

clue.text: 'Solvers need this book' (The Sun's ruling)

parts.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god
a ruling party is in power

explanation.surface: An advert insists solvers need a book, citing the Sun newspaper's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Power is one of the theme's Wills.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword solvers need mental capacity and intelligence to crack the clues.

clue.text: Speculator upped price in respect of army rations?

parts.note: a bull is a speculator betting on rising prices

indicators.note: in a down clue upped means turned upwards, so the words read bottom to top

parts.note: a fee is a price
by can mean in respect of, as in 'by name'

explanation.surface: A market speculator puts up the price of army supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' reverses FEE + BY to make YBEEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned corned meat was a staple ration for soldiers in both World Wars.

clue.text: Member of iconic English group, the inspiration for 'Come Together'?

definitions.text: Member of iconic English group, the inspiration for 'Come Together'?

parts.words: Member of iconic English group, the inspiration for 'Come Together'
parts.note: the red double-decker of the capital is famous for none turning up for ages, then several arriving together

explanation.surface: A question about which Beatle inspired the song Come Together.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Beatles and their song; the 'group' is a fleet of red double-deckers, and the joke is that you wait ages, then three come along at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The red double-decker is an iconic vehicle of the capital, notorious for arriving in clusters.

clue.text: French city herald-in-chief

definitions.meaning: the city on the Rhone, France's third largest
Lord ___ King of Arms is Scotland's chief herald

explanation.surface: A French city's chief town crier.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland's top heraldic official has the title Lord ___ King of Arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city name is also the title of Scotland's chief heraldic officer.

clue.text: Support for nautical types given to anxiety about lugger's bow

indicators.note: the word for given to anxiety goes around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: caring means concerned, prone to worry on others' behalf

indicators.note: a bow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of lugger is taken

explanation.surface: Sailors who worry a lot fret over the front of their lugger, a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Carling, England rugby captain, is one of the theme's Wills.
explanation.definitionFit: In shipbuilding this is a short fore-and-aft timber between deck beams, supporting the deck sailors stand on.

clue.text: Old dealer in game, maybe Texas hold'em, blowing a thousand in the last cut

indicators.note: the shortened month term is placed in the game minus its thousand
blowing means squandering, so the thousand is lost from the card game

parts.note: Texas hold'em is an example of poker
K is short for a thousand

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so only the first letters of the word are kept

parts.note: ultimo means of last month

explanation.surface: A gambler loses a thousand at Texas hold'em, the poker game, in the final round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' leaves POER; 'cut' and 'in' handle the last-month term 'ult.', from commercial letters. 'game' means game birds, not cards. Will Poulter is a theme actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a poulterer, a trader in fowl and game birds.

clue.text: Red mark remaining following cut

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin

indicators.note: the letter for following is cut out of the word for remaining

parts.note: left means remaining, as in 'what's left'
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A red mark is left after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes F from LEFT to leave LET. Will Scarlet is one of Robin Hood's men, in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant crimson colour is a shade of red.

clue.text: Just reconnected parts of 16

indicators.note: the letters of the other answer are joined back together in a different order

parts.note: the answer to 16 across, the French city

explanation.surface: Someone has just put back together pieces of the other clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely or simply, as in 'only a child', means just.

clue.text: Island folk re-routing river at mouth, as I can do

indicators.note: sending along a new route, so the letters travel a different order
the mouth of the word river is its first letter

explanation.surface: A river engineer boasts of diverting the waterway at its estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-routing' shuffles R with AS I CAN DO.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Orkney, the Scottish islands, are known by this Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Sum from Descartes written just after midnight?

definitions.meaning: in 'cogito ergo sum', the Latin sum means this first-person phrase
1 a.m. written down looks like this, an hour after midnight

explanation.surface: A philosophical calculation dashed off in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sum' looks arithmetical but is Latin from 'I think, therefore...'; the numeral 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin sum translates as the first-person present of 'to be'; 1 a.m. looks the same.

clue.text: What Bill looks like from behind?

definitions.text: What Bill looks like from behind?

indicators.note: read from behind means read from the end back to the start

parts.note: neb is a dialect word for a bird's bill or beak

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a man named Bill looks like from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and his partner were the Flowerpot Men of the old BBC children's show, so Bill's reversed beak gives his pal.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's TV show Bill always had his twin flowerpot puppet alongside, so viewed backwards Bill becomes his partner.

clue.text: Brilliant satirist exercises to rear of chamber

indicators.note: the exercise letters sit behind, after, the chamber

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A clever comic writer works out behind a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander, the eighteenth-century poet of The Dunciad, is one of English literature's great satirists.

clue.text: Cry with laughter swapping tops, not a patch on anybody else?

definitions.text: not a patch on anybody else?

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words change places

parts.note: mirth is laughter
a bark is a cry, as from a dog

explanation.surface: Someone weeps with laughter, unlike anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a patch on' usually means inferior; here it is a skin patch on nobody else, as each one is unique.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural blemish on the skin is a patch that is yours alone, found on nobody else.

clue.text: A half-day's cycling injury

indicators.note: moving round in a cycle, so the front letter goes to the back
the first half of the day name is taken

explanation.surface: An accident during half a day's bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A half' of the weekday gives THUR; 'cycling' moves the T to the end. William Hurt, the actor, fits the Will theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or pain suffered, as in 'no lasting harm done', is a noun for injury.

clue.text: Great body, Octopussy!

definitions.meaning: a large host or multitude of people, as in 'a whole host of fans'
a playful adjective: an octopus is full of arms, like a hairy beast is full of hair

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the physique of the Bond girl Octopussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Octopussy' is the Bond film, but here it means an octopus, whose eight limbs make it, jokily, well endowed with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast multitude is a host; and something with many limbs is, jokingly, full of arms.

clue.text: Spouse of thematic Royal immersed in classwork at Eton

indicators.note: plunged inside, so the name lies buried in the words classwork at Eton

explanation.surface: A royal spouse busy with homework at the famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Wills, and Prince William, who went to Eton, is the royal; his wife is the Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Princess of Wales, née Middleton, married Prince William in 2011.

clue.text: Right wingers in politics, the portrayal of 12

definitions.note: 12 across, whose answer means the sense of one's identity

indicators.note: the right-hand wing, the last letter, of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Political figures on the right are portrayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right wingers' looks political; it means the right-hand end letters. Will Self, the novelist, is a theme member.
explanation.definitionFit: One's own person or identity is a synonym of the 12 answer, the conscious 'I'.

clue.text: TV actor's son picks up story on radio

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: spoken on the radio, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a myth is a story

explanation.surface: An actor's son listens to a radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Reece, of The League of Gentlemen, is the actor; Will Smith also fits the Will theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Reece of Inside No. 9 and The League of Gentlemen is a British television performer.
